doc_name: Ghosts (What We Do in the Shadows)
text: "Ghosts" is the second episode of the second season of the American mockumentary comedy horror series What We Do in the Shadows, set in Staten Island, New York City, and serves as the twelfth overall episode of the series. Written by executive producer Paul Simms and directed by producer Kyle Newacheck, it premiered on FX on April 15, 2020, airing back-to-back with the previous episode, "Resurrection." The episode follows the lives of three vampires—Nandor, Laszlo, and Nadja—alongside Colin Robinson, an energy vampire, and Guillermo, Nandor's familiar. The vampires become disturbed by ghosts and decide to help them resolve their unfinished business so they can move on. Initially, the vampires believe Guillermo is responsible for the disturbances, but Nadja concludes that ghosts—dead beings with unresolved matters—are present in the house. She conducts a séance that reveals Gregor (Jake McDorman), who annoys Laszlo (Matt Berry). The vampires perform another séance to see their past selves; Laszlo and Nadja bond with their former versions, while Nandor (Kayvan Novak) struggles to speak his extinct ancestral language. Nadja allows her ghost self to stay and has her possess one of her dolls, instructing her not to reveal the situation to the others. Nandor eventually learns that his ghost wants to reconnect with his warrior horse, which he killed out of starvation; through a séance, they summon the horse, and both disappear after completing their unfinished business. Laszlo helps his ghost self orgasm, as Nadja turned him into a vampire during sex before he could ejaculate. Colin Robinson (Mark Proksch) conjures his dead grandmother to tell her an "updog" joke, then vanishes her after she laughs. FX confirmed in March 2020 that the episode would be titled "Ghosts," with Simms receiving his third writing credit and Newacheck his second directing credit. In its original American broadcast, "Ghosts" was seen by an estimated 0.409 million household viewers with a 0.17 ratings share among adults aged 18–49, representing a 24% decrease from the previous episode, which reached 0.537 million viewers with a 0.22 share. With DVR factored in, the episode was watched by 0.915 million viewers with a 0.3 share in the 18–49 demographic. The episode received positive critical reviews, with Katie Rife of The A.V. Club giving it a "B" and praising its ambition, humor, and special effects, including faux-medieval paintings of Nandor. Tony Sokol of Den of Geek awarded it 4.5 out of 5 stars, calling it an "almost historic" episode and highlighting the expansion of the monster universe and the recurring guest formerly-Jeff, who is set to return. Greg Wheeler of The Review Geek gave it 3.5 out of 5 stars, noting the episode's strong character development and memorable jokes, with the fate of Nadja's ghost possessing her doll remaining unresolved. Paul Simms was nominated for Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series at the 72nd Primetime Emmy Awards but lost to Schitt's Creek for the episode "Happy Ending."
